questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with South Sudan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture South Sudan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the South Sudan article.

questions.proof: The country is bordered by Ethiopia to the east; Kenya to the southeast; Uganda to the south; the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the southwest; the Central African Republic to the west; and the Republic of Sudan to the north.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of South Sudan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the South Sudan article.

questions.proof: There are over 60 indigenous languages in South Sudan, along with English (the country's official language) and Arabic.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Just two years after South Sudan gained its independence, in _____, a civil war began.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the South Sudan article.

questions.proof: Just two years after South Sudan gained its independence, in 2013, a civil war began.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Only three countries in the world scored lower: Central African Republic, _____, and Chad.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Republic”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the South Sudan article, under the heading “People”.

questions.proof: Only three countries in the world scored lower: Central African Republic, Nigeria, and Chad.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This part of the British Empire became the Republic of Sudan when independence was achieved in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the South Sudan article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: This part of the British Empire became the Republic of Sudan when independence was achieved in 1956.
